Title: MIRROR: Novelty-Constrained Memory-Guided MCTS Red-Teaming for Agentic RAG
Abstract: Multimodal agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems expand the attack surface beyond prompt injection to include text poisoning, image injection, direct-query attacks, and orchestrator-level tool manipulation. Existing red-teaming approaches are typically surface-specific and often recycle known attack templates; on text-poisoning benchmarks we measure 73-84% exact duplication. We present MIRROR, a unified cross-surface framework that performs memory-guided Monte Carlo tree search while conditioning candidate generation on retrieved context under an explicit novelty constraint. A deterministic Novelty Gate rejects any candidate matching the retrieval set under normalized comparison, allowing retrieval to inform search priors without enabling prompt copying. Across four attack surfaces on a multimodal agentic RAG target, MIRROR attains 76% ASR on image poisoning compared with 52% for baselines, 97% ASR on orchestrator attacks at half the query cost, and the lowest cross-surface variance (coefficient of variation 0.47). In contrast, specialized baselines collapse across surfaces: suffix optimization reaches 79% ASR on text poisoning but 1% on direct queries. We release ART-SafeBench with 41,815 in-package records and runtime adapters yielding 41,991+ total records across four surfaces.
Major_Contribution_Result: MIRROR is a cross-surface red-teaming framework for multimodal agentic RAG that uses memory-guided Monte Carlo tree search with a deterministic Novelty Gate to block exact duplicates of retrieved attack templates. The authors report that existing approaches often recycle templates (73–84% exact duplication on text-poisoning benchmarks). Across four surfaces on a multimodal agentic RAG target, MIRROR attains 76% ASR on image poisoning versus 52% for baselines, 97% ASR on orchestrator attacks at half the query cost, and the lowest cross-surface variance (CV 0.47), with 0% DupBench@Exact on B1 in the conclusion setting. They release ART-SafeBench (41,815 in-package records; 41,991+ with runtime adapters).
Research_Limitations_Challenges: In Limitations and scope, the authors report a CYBERRAG case study where baselines outperform MIRROR under structured-output/domain-shift constraints, isolating corpus–target alignment and simulator fidelity as binding factors. Novelty Gate/DupBench are exact-match under stated normalizations; semantic paraphrases can still pass. Strict one-factor ablations over priors, gating, and verification remain future work. B2 novelty metrics are not applicable to image carriers under their text-based duplication procedure. On B1, specialized suffix search (GCG) can attain higher ASR; MIRROR is positioned as complementary.
Critics: This is an automated red-teaming/evaluation-methods paper for multimodal agentic RAG, emphasizing novelty-aware ASR rather than a defense lifecycle. Reported ASR gains are target- and surface-specific (and can reverse under domain shift), so they should not be treated as universal agent vulnerability rates. It strengthens evaluation methodology (novelty/duplication diagnostics) but does not claim gate-complete mitigation or reassessment for general tool agents.
